title: Create Azure SQL from C#
description: Provision an Azure SQL Database server and database programmatically with the Azure.ResourceManager.Sql package.

data.text: You can create Azure SQL resources from C# using the Azure management SDK. This is useful for automated provisioning in setup scripts, tests, or multi-tenant applications.

data.title: Install Azure.ResourceManager.Sql
data.content: Add the NuGet package for Azure SQL management.

data.title: Provision an Azure SQL server and database
data.content: Use the Azure management SDK with DefaultAzureCredential.

data.title: Authentication
data.text: For management-plane operations, your identity needs the Contributor role on the resource group. For data-plane operations like connecting from EF Core, use a database user or managed identity.
Azure SQL blocks external connections by default. Create a firewall rule to allow your IP or Azure services.

data.title: Create a firewall rule
data.content: Allow Azure services to reach the SQL server.

data.title: Provision a database from a setup script
data.description: Write a small C# console app that creates an Azure SQL server and database.
steps: Create a console app and add `Azure.ResourceManager.Sql`
Create a SQL server with admin credentials
Create a database with serverless General Purpose SKU
Print the fully qualified database name
data.expectedOutcome: A new SQL server and database appear in the Azure portal.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Firewall rules control network access to Azure SQL
Prefer Azure AD authentication for management operations
Management SDK operations are async and long-running
data.takeaway: Automating database creation with C# removes manual portal steps and keeps infrastructure aligned with your application lifecycle.
